;Armed conflicts and attacks
*[[Ituri conflict]]
**The [[Armed Forces of the Democratic Republic of the Congo|army]] of the [[Democratic Republic of the Congo]] says it killed 33 militiamen and reported the death of two soldiers in days of intense fighting in [[Ituri province]]. The army says it seized control of two rebel strongholds held by the Cooperative for the Development of Congo (CODECO) group, which is accused by the [[United Nations]] of committing [[war crime]]s. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-congo-security/congo-army-says-it-killed-33-militiaman-in-days-of-intense-fighting-idUSKBN27D1PT?il=0 (Reuters)]
*[[War in Afghanistan (2001–2021)|War in Afghanistan]]
**Over 100 [[Taliban]] insurgents are killed as the [[Afghan Armed Forces]] retake parts of [[Helmand Province]]. [https://tolonews.com/index.php/afghanistan-167357 (TOLO News)]
*[[2020 Nagorno-Karabakh conflict]], [[Barda ballistic missile attacks]]
**[[Azerbaijan]] says the death toll from an [[Armed Forces of Armenia|Armenian]] [[Cluster munition|cluster missile]] attack on [[Barda, Azerbaijan|Barda]] has risen to 21 with dozens more wounded. Armenia denies carrying out the strike. [https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/world-europe-54722120 (BBC News)]

;Business and economy
*[[Germany|German]] anti-trust regulator [[Federal Cartel Office]] launches an investigation into [[Amazon (company)|Amazon]] and [[Apple Inc.|Apple]] for potentially breaking [[Competition law|competition laws]], by having the former being the exclusive distributor for the latter's dealerships online. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-amazon-com-germany-competition/german-watchdog-launches-new-investigation-into-amazon-report-idUSKBN27D2OO?il=0 (Reuters)]

;Disasters and accidents
*[[2020 Atlantic hurricane season]]
**[[President of the United States|U.S. President]] [[Donald Trump]] declares a [[state of emergency]] for [[Louisiana]] ahead of [[Hurricane Zeta]]'s impending landfall. [https://www.foxnews.com/weather/zeta-re-strengthens-into-a-hurricane-expected-to-bring-a-life-threatening-storm-surge-to-louisiana (Fox News)]
**The [[National Hurricane Center]] forecasts {{convert|5|-|8|ft|m}} of storm surge for the entire [[Mississippi]] coastline. In Louisiana, mandatory evacuations are issued in [[Terrebonne Parish, Louisiana|Terrebonne Parish]] and [[Jefferson Parish, Louisiana|Jefferson Parish]]. [[Alabama]] [[List of governors of Alabama|Governor]] [[Kay Ivey]] and [[Mississippi]] [[List of governors of Mississippi|Governor]] [[Tate Reeves]] issue a [[state of emergency]] for their states. [https://www.cnn.com/2020/10/28/us/hurricane-zeta-wednesday/index.html (CNN)]
**The [[National Weather Service]] issues [[Tropical cyclone warnings and watches |Storm Surge Warnings]] from the mouth of the [[Atchafalaya River]], [[Louisiana]], to [[Navarre, Florida]]. [https://www.nhc.noaa.gov/text/refresh/MIATCPAT3+shtml/281141.shtml? (National Hurricane Center)]
**Hurricane Zeta strengthens to a Category 2 hurricane. [https://www.nhc.noaa.gov/archive/2020/al28/al282020.public_a.016.shtml? (National Hurricane Center)]
**Hurricane Zeta makes landfall near [[Cocodrie, Louisiana]], as a [[Category 2 hurricane]] with sustained winds of 110 mph. In the process, it sets a new record for being the fifth named storm to make landfall in [[Louisiana]] in a single season, the previous record being four. [https://www.nytimes.com/2020/10/28/us/hurricane-zeta.html (''The New York Times'')]

;Health and environment 
*[[COVID-19 pandemic]]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Europe]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Germany]]
****The [[Robert Koch Institute]] reports a record 14,964 new infections in the past 24 hours, putting the total number of cases at 464,239. [https://www.welt.de/vermischtes/article206504969/Corona-RKI-meldet-Rekord-bei-Neuinfektionen-in-Deutschland-14-964-Faelle.html (''Welt'')]
****[[Chancellor of Germany|Chancellor]] [[Angela Merkel]] and leaders of 16 [[States of Germany|states]] agree to impose a nationwide partial lockdown from November 2, which means that restaurants, bars, and all leisure facilities are ordered to be closed until November 30, private gatherings will be limited to ten people and social contacts will be limited to two households. However, schools, churches and kindergartens will remain open with strict hygiene measures. The new restrictions will last for at least four weeks. [https://www.france24.com/en/europe/20201028-german-officials-agree-on-partial-lockdown-to-curb-mounting-covid-19-cases (France 24)] [https://edition.cnn.com/2020/10/28/europe/europe-new-lockdowns-announced-intl/index.html (CNN)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Switzerland]]
****[[Switzerland]]'s [[Federal Office of Public Health]] reports a record of 8,616 new infections in the last 24 hours, bringing the total to 135,658. In addition, in the last two weeks, the positivity rate has risen from 14% to 32%, higher than the peak of 26% during the first wave. [https://lenews.ch/2020/10/28/coronavirus-a-record-8600-new-daily-cases-in-switzerland/ (''Le News'')]
****Switzerland imposes new restrictions, ordering dance clubs to be closed beginning tomorrow, halting in-person university classes beginning in early November, and placing new limits on sporting and leisure activities. In addition, a requirement to wear masks in all offices and secondary schools as well as outdoors where [[social distancing]] is difficult has been indefinitely extended. [https://finance.yahoo.com/news/swiss-enact-restrictions-mask-rules-151501721.html (Yahoo! Finance)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in the Czech Republic]]
****The [[Czech Republic]] reports 15,663 new cases, a record number since the [[pandemic]] began, as the country struggles with one of Europe's fastest growing infection rates. [https://www.arabnews.com/node/1755216/world (''Arab News'')]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in France]]
****[[President of France|French President]] [[Emmanuel Macron]] announces a second nationwide [[COVID-19 pandemic lockdowns|lockdown]] from October 30, with all non-essential businesses ordered to close. Unlike the first lockdown in March, most schools and factories will remain open and care home visits will still be allowed. [https://www.bbc.com/news/world-europe-54716993 (BBC News)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Greece]]
****[[Greece]] reports a record 1,547 new cases, bringing the nationwide total to 34,299 cases, according to data from [[National Public Health Organization (Greece)|National Public Health Organization]]. [https://eody.gov.gr/20201028_briefing_covid19/ (NPHO)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Italy]]
****[[Italy]] registers a record 24,991 new infections over the past 24 hours, according to [[Ministry of Health (Italy)|health ministry]] data, bringing the nationwide total of cases to 589,766. [https://amp.rte.ie/amp/1174511/ (RTÉ)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Poland]]
****[[Poland]] reports 18,820 new cases and 236 new deaths in the last 24 hours. It is the largest jump in the number of cases and the deadliest day since the start of the pandemic, bringing the total number of cases to 299,049. [https://www.reuters.com/article/health-coronavirus-poland/update-1-poland-reports-record-rise-in-daily-coronavirus-cases-and-deaths-idINL1N2HJ0MU (Reuters)] [https://polandin.com/50536305/covid19-recordbreaking-18820-new-infections-in-poland (Poland In)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Portugal]]
****[[Portugal]] reports a record daily increase with 3,960 new cases, bringing the cumulative counts to 128,382 confirmed cases and 2,395 deaths. [https://covid19.min-saude.pt/wp-content/uploads/2020/10/240_DGS_boletim_20201028.pdf (DGS)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Russia]]
****[[Russia]] reports a record high of 346 new fatalities in the last 24 hours, pushing the national death toll to 26,935. [https://www.themoscowtimes.com/2020/10/28/russia-sets-new-single-day-coronavirus-deaths-record-a71880 (''The Moscow Times'')]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Slovenia]]
****[[Slovenia]] reports 2,605 new cases, a new record since the start of the pandemic. [https://english.sta.si/2824833/slovenia-confirms-2-605-new-coronavirus-cases-highest-daily-figure-so-far (STA)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Sweden]]
****[[Sweden]] reports 1,980 new infections in the past 24 hours, its highest number in a single day yet, bringing the nationwide total at 117,913. [https://www.reuters.com/article/health-coronavirus-sweden-cases/sweden-sets-new-daily-covid-19-case-record-as-infections-surge-idUSL8N2HJ5RE (Reuters)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Turkey]]
****[[Turkey]] surpasses 10,000 COVID-19 deaths, becoming the eighth European country to reach the milestone. [https://www.aa.com.tr/en/latest-on-coronavirus-outbreak/coronavirus-deaths-in-turkey-exceed-10-000/2022746 (Anadolu Agency)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Ukraine]]
****[[Ukraine]] reports a record high of 165 fatalities in the last 24 hours, bringing the nationwide death toll to 6,755. [https://gordonua.com/news/society/za-sutki-v-ukraine-podtverdili-pochti-75-tys-novyh-sluchaev-covid-19-1524914.html (Gordonua)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Asia]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Indonesia]]
****[[Indonesia]] surpasses 400,000 total cases of COVID-19, becoming the first country in [[Southeast Asia]] to reach the milestone. [https://www.cnnindonesia.com/nasional/20201028120808-20-563649/bertambah-4029-kasus-positif-covid-19-tembus-400-ribu (CNN Indonesia)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Iran]]
****[[Iran]] reports a record 415 new fatalities, bringing the death toll since the pandemic began to 33,714. [https://www.barrons.com/news/iran-reports-single-day-record-415-virus-deaths-01603884303 (''Barron's'')]
****Iran's [[List of speakers of the Parliament of Iran|parliamentary speaker]] [[Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf]] tested positive for COVID-19. [https://www.voanews.com/middle-east/iran-parliament-speaker-contracts-virus-deaths-surge (Voice of America)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Thailand]]
****[[Thailand]]'s [[cabinet of Thailand|cabinet]] agrees to extend a [[state of emergency]] until the end of November to contain its COVID-19 outbreak. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-health-coronavirus-thailand/thai-emergency-decree-extended-to-end-november-to-curb-coronavirus-idUSKBN27D0VM (Reuters)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in the United States]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in New York (state)]]
****[[New York (state)|New York]] surpasses 500,000 total confirmed COVID-19 cases, becoming the fourth state to surpass that number after [[California]], [[Florida]] and [[Texas]]. [https://www.nbcnewyork.com/news/coronavirus/new-york-nears-a-half-million-confirmed-covid-cases-as-cluster-battle-continues/2691260/ (WNBC-TV)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Oceania]]
***[[Tonga]] extends the state of emergency, which includes curfews and restrictions on gatherings, until November 23. The country, which is COVID-19-free, imposed strict measures on March 12. [https://www.rnz.co.nz/international/pacific-news/429321/tonga-further-extends-state-of-emergency (RNZ)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in South Africa]]
***[[President of South Africa|President]] [[Cyril Ramaphosa]] goes into self-quarantine after one of 35 guests at a charity event that he attended tested positive for COVID-19. [https://www.sowetanlive.co.za/news/south-africa/2020-10-28-cyril-ramaphosa-goes-into-self-isolation/ (Sowetanlive)]

;International relations
*[[France–Turkey relations]]
**[[Turkey]] threatens to take "legal and diplomatic action" in response to [[France|French]] magazine ''[[Charlie Hebdo]]'''s [[caricature]] mocking [[President of Turkey|Turkish President]] [[Recep Tayyip Erdoğan]]. Turkish Vice President [[Fuat Oktay]] condemns the publication. France responds by saying that the country would not give in to "destabilisation and intimidation attempts." [https://www.france24.com/en/europe/20201028-turkey-blasts-charlie-hebdo-s-immoral-caricature-of-erdogan (France 24)]

;Law and crime
*[[2020–2021 United States racial unrest]], [[Black Lives Matter]]
**Protesters march through [[Philadelphia]] for a second night, demanding racial justice after the [[killing of Walter Wallace]]. The marches began peacefully but became more confrontational into the evening and Wednesday morning. Police and the city's office of emergency management said looting was reported in several areas. Protesters try to erect makeshift barricades using bins while police use [[pepper spray]] and [[police baton|batons]] after saying they were attacked by demonstrators. [https://www.bbc.com/news/world-us-canada-54710244 (BBC News)]
*[[Gretchen Whitmer kidnapping plot]]
**An unsealed search warrant reveals that Barry Croft, one of the suspects accused in federal court of plotting to [[kidnap]] [[Governor of Michigan|Michigan Governor]] [[Gretchen Whitmer]], has also discussed [[Governor of South Carolina|South Carolina Governor]] [[Henry McMaster]] and [[President of the United States|President]] [[Donald Trump]] as possible targets. [https://www.detroitnews.com/story/news/local/michigan/2020/10/28/militia-member-helped-feds-infiltrate-whitmer-kidnap-crew-fbi-says/6060368002/ (''The Detroit News'')] [https://www.postandcourier.com/columbia/news/sc-gov-mcmaster-was-target-of-group-accused-of-plotting-to-kidnap-michigan-governor/article_36a665a4-196d-11eb-a91c-0ffded180433.html (''The Post and Courier'')]
*The [[Federal Bureau of Investigation|FBI]] arrests five people in the United States, and charges three more, for spying on opponents of the [[Chinese Communist Party]] and trying, among other things, to coerce them to return home to face trial. [https://www.bbc.com/news/world-us-canada-54724471 (BBC News)]

;Politics and elections
*[[2020 Tanzanian general election]]
**[[Tanzanians]] head to the polls to elect their [[President of Tanzania|President]]. Incumbent [[John Magufuli]] seeks reelection as his top opposition candidate [[Tundu Lissu]], who returned from [[exile]] after a failed [[assassination]] attempt, warns of "widespread irregularities". [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2020/10/28/tanzania-votes-for-president-amid-fears-of-violence-fraud (Al Jazeera)]

[https://www.gazetaprawna.pl/artykuly/1494857,komendant-glowny-policji-o-protestach-zatrzymano-blisko-80-osob-prowadzonych-jest-ponad-100-postepowan-ws-dewastacji.html (''Gazeta Prawna'')]
